items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: He was hanging out with Coltrane

ctx.x: I’ve had students who come to me with things they’ve learned from other teachers or perhaps on the Internet and they ask about certain harmonic things that I never use. And so I’m wondering how to deal with that?

Well what happens is these kids are also getting on the Internet and getting tons of information and getting there’s — I think it’s sensory overload, the amount of information that they can get. So I slow them down and I just tell them okay, let’s slow down and I let them know, you know, you’re going to have to learn how to play by ear. You’re going to have to. I tell them you’ve got to learn all these scales, you’re going to learn all these patterns, you’re going to get the sound of this under your fingers. When…

together for these Blue Note sessions which they really just — these were not working bands. They got together, looked at the music and went in. But at that point they were speaking to each other in such a highly sophisticated fashion that they could hear through things. They could hear through things.
